column1: # boot-doc-registry.tsv — WHICH boot/lifecycle documents exist, and the only copy.
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
# The set of these documents is written down TWICE, in two languages, with no
# compiler between them: `bootDocRegistry` (server/ocserverd/api_bootdocs.go)
# decides what the server serves, and the cockpit carries its own list so it can
# give each one a row, a name and an icon in the settings page.
# A divergence produces NO error anywhere. It produces a document that ships,
# that the server serves, and that the owner simply cannot see — no blank page,
# no 404, nothing to notice. That is the exact failure this whole ticket was
# opened for, and every prose list of these kinds ever written in this tree went
# stale in that direction.
# Both sides are checked against THIS table, so a drift names the side that
# drifted instead of merely reporting that two things differ. Deliberately NOT a
# mock of one side inside the other's test — that would only prove the mock
# agrees with itself.
# WHAT A CHANGE HERE COSTS
# Shipping a document means editing this file in the SAME commit as the registry
# row. That is the point: the edit is one line, and skipping it is a red test
# rather than an invisible hole.
# COLUMNS
# kind          the document-history kind — the first half of its address
# key           the second half; a kind serving more than one has one row each
# read_only     true when no caller may edit it (every write face answers 405)
# What is NOT here: caps, seed filenames, variables, whether it carries a
# read-only head. Those are per-side implementation and adding them would make
# this a second registry rather than a list of what exists.
